executiveSummary: GM0753 passes the complete deterministic contract over all ten canonical scenarios, T+0/6/12/24/48/72 and all eight essential services. Its 2025 CBS identity, generalized boundary, headline demography, 19 neighbourhoods, one BAG place, three BRT settlements, Best station, six NWB logical links, null semantics, local reconciliation, causal ledgers, exact zero-intensity behavior and sustained-water repair guard are coherent. Release remains correction-required for three high-severity spatial defects. First, the named Rhine, Meuse and IJssel preset assigns Best sustained direct municipality-wide inundation stress even though the current Brabant-Zuidoost risk profile says the high-lying region has no direct flood danger and identifies only indirect large-river effects when northern flooding prevents southern drainage. Internal inundation stress reaches 0.9464 at T+12 and remains there through T+72, producing 11,349 modeled people under pressure and 769,635 cumulative event-attributable essential-service person-hours at T+72. Second, the neighbourhood water map contradicts Best's own 70 mm/hour stress test: Villawijk ranks third despite being the one mapped result the municipality did not recognize in practice, while documented Breeven, Wilhelminadorp and Speelheide rank seventeenth through nineteenth. The same seed order is reused for river, storm, heat, winter, cyber and wildfire; this also puts officially identified hot Breeven seventeenth. Third, a focused synthetic fire source at the official centre of Heide makes the source neighbourhood rank sixth while Aarlesche Erven 2.745 km away ranks first. Best's unique 2.6 km rail tunnel and underground station are present only as a station point, not a tunnel/evacuation dependency. Public context usefully identifies nine De Dommel weirs, provider responsibility and nearby external acute hospitals, but none causally changes the simulation. Physical Enexis, Brabant Water, sewer, telecom, care, supply and emergency topology, live state, backups, stocks, crews and restoration commitments remain unavailable or security-sensitive and were not invented.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK
evidenceSources.title: Kerncijfers wijken en buurten 2025 and Gemeente gegeneraliseerd 2025 — GM0753
supports: Machine-readable official-context identity and annual statistics: GM0753/Best, 31,652 residents, density 934 per square kilometre, 6,561 residents aged 65 or older and 4,397 one-person households.

The companion annual generalized municipality and neighbourhood polygons at https://api.pdok.nl/cbs/gebiedsindelingen/ogc/v1 are CC BY 4.0 and provide the administrative geometry consumed by the application.
CBS rounded or suppressed neighbourhood values require explicit null and reconciliation semantics; administrative boundaries are not hazard, catchment, provider or incident footprints.

evidenceSources.title: Regionaal Risicoprofiel 2025–2028, definitief versie 1.0
supports: Best is one of the 21 municipalities in Brabant-Zuidoost. The profile says the region's relatively high position means there is no direct flood danger; a large-river dike breach north of the region can instead prevent water draining from southern Brabant.

The regional all-hazard analysis covers high river water, extreme precipitation, defence failure, wildfire, winter weather, heat, storm, loss of electricity, gas/heat, telecom, drinking water and wastewater, cyberattack and cascading vital-process dependencies.

The profile identifies Best's 2.6 km rail tunnel, including 900 m enclosed, 200 m depressed open track and its underground station, as the region's only rail tunnel of this class and records dedicated response planning.
It also identifies Eindhoven Airport, roads, rail, vital-object access, hospitals, utilities and food supply as linked regional consequences of storm and winter weather.

The strategic profile is a static four-year risk analysis, not a live warning, event footprint, asset state, probability feed or GM0753 restoration estimate; no explicit dataset reuse licence is stated.

evidenceSources.title: Klimaatstresstesten Best
supports: The official local test maps water on streets for a 70 mm in one hour climate shower and names Centrum, Naastenbest, Wilhelminadorp, Het Zand, Speelheide, De Leeuwerik, Breeven, Heide and Villawijk as having water against buildings.

The municipality says it recognizes mapped water-on-street locations from practice except the Villawijk result. Salderes, Heuveleind, Heivelden, Dijkstraten and Steegsche Velden mainly retain water on roads, verges, gardens and other public space.
Its urban heat-island analysis ranges from 0.05 to 3.5 degrees Celsius and names industrial areas 't Zand, Breeven and Heide, the area west of Salderes, and Centrum/Oud Best as the hottest areas.

Best lies on sand with relatively deep groundwater. The document identifies soil-moisture, green-space, nature, agriculture, water-availability and water-quality impacts and projects a 10–25 cm fall in average lowest groundwater level in the north under its WH2050 comparison.
This is authoritative scenario/context and presentation mapping, not an observed current event, live feed or licensed native GIS surface; no fixed refresh cadence or explicit reuse licence is stated.

evidenceSources.title: Regionaal Crisisplan 2024–2027
supports: The plan explicitly treats a short acute crisis as lasting up to about three days and allows transition to a long-crisis structure, directly matching the simulator's first-72-hour focus.
Monitoring and signalering are continuous; acute threats can trigger CoPI or ROT, while a planning staff builds a shared multidisciplinary picture for a concrete threat.

The mayor or safety-region chair holds authority for general public-order and safety measures such as evacuation, while functional-chain authority for electricity, food safety and other sectors remains with the responsible minister or national body.

It defines roles and coordination, not deterministic intervention effects, staffing, stocks, service restoration times or a machine-readable operational incident feed; it is updated when policy-cycle reasons arise and states no dataset reuse licence.

evidenceSources.title: Nationaal Wegenbestand Wegen and Spoorwegen OGC APIs
evidenceSources.edition: NWB application snapshot 2026-08-01; ProRail snapshot retrieved 2026-09-02
supports: NWB is machine-readable national road-section geometry under CC0 1.0 with monthly updates; the generated Best graph resolves A2, A50, A58 and N620 boundary links.
The companion ProRail OGC API at https://api.pdok.nl/prorail/spoorwegen/ogc/v1 provides traces and stations under CC0 1.0 with manual updates; Best station is inside GM0753.
These static geometries do not establish live closure, congestion, rail operation, tunnel system state, emergency access, evacuation throughput or utility capacity.

evidenceSources.publisher: Het Waterschapshuis / Dutch water boards via PDOK
evidenceSources.title: Waterschappen Kunstwerken IMWA and Waterketen DAMO OGC APIs
supports: Machine-readable official object context under CC BY-SA 4.0; the current generalized-boundary intersection contains nine realized weirs managed by Waterschap De Dommel and no DAMO sewer pump or treatment plant.
The Kunstwerken service declares weekly updates; contributor and collection completeness vary, so retrieval and object timestamps must be retained.
Object presence or absence does not establish complete municipal drainage inventory, hydraulic connectivity, control logic, live status, emergency power, capacity or restoration time.

evidenceSources.title: RIVM Vragenlijst aanbod SEH’s en Acute Verloskunde 2026, version 1.1
supports: Annual machine-readable hospital questionnaire data are public under CC0 1.0 and identify emergency-department offer, 24/7 status, reported treatment rooms and prior-year visits.

No listed acute-care hospital lies inside GM0753; nearest by straight-line reference-point distance are Catharina Ziekenhuis in Eindhoven at 7.52 km and Máxima Medisch Centrum in Veldhoven at 12.34 km, both reporting 24/7 emergency departments.
The data are dated context, not live occupancy, staffing, diversion, ambulance travel time, generator endurance, incident acceptance or restoration commitment.

evidenceSources.title: Precipitation — radar 5 minute reflectivity composites over the Netherlands, version 2.0
supports: Machine-readable Open Data API, MQTT and WMS access to a national five-minute radar composite under CC BY 4.0; the application retains observation/retrieval time and displays it as observed context.
The current cached image is not aligned to the scenario clock, does not drive simulated rain, and is not a 72-hour forecast; radar can also contain missing values and artefacts.
An event adapter can use the feed for time-stamped nowcast/observation context only after explicit spatial/temporal matching, never as retrospective evidence for an arbitrary exercise.

transport.summary: Best station and six Dutch road links are structurally valid, but the graph omits the documented tunnel semantics and uses generalized logical capacity.
notes: Six links connect Oirschot, Boxtel, Eindhoven and Son en Breugel: A58 lengths 0.287 and 1.194 km, A2 lengths 3.853 and 1.641 km, A50 length 1.395 km and N620 length 0.851 km.
Five trunk links use nominal capacity 260 and N620 uses 150, totaling 1,450 scenario units in every service view. These are not measured road, rail or utility capacity.
ProRail identifies Best station inside the boundary and static transit data contribute 37 stop areas.
The model has no tunnel edge, enclosed/depressed section, evacuation path, ventilation/safety-system state or rail-service capacity for the unique Best tunnel documented by E02.

emergencyContext.summary: Authoritative context identifies water controls, provider responsibility, external acute-care dependence, crisis roles and Best's tunnel, but operational state is absent.
notes: The public water snapshot contributes nine De Dommel weirs and no sewer pump/RWZI inside GM0753; this is partial context, not proof that other municipal assets do not exist.

Live Stichting Mijn Aansluiting point queries returned Enexis for electricity and gas, Brabant Water for drinking water and Ziggo for fixed media; drainage returned no polygon. These provider territories are non-causal responsibility context.

The cached KVK/PDOK registry contributes eight coarse government-service locations, including two public-order-and-safety records, but their 2020 registration does not establish emergency role, opening, staffing or capacity.

No RIVM 2026 acute hospital lies inside the boundary; Catharina Ziekenhuis and Máxima Medisch Centrum are the nearest listed 24/7 emergency departments, but route and acceptance state are not modeled.
No sensitive physical topology, live utility/transport/facility state, backup endurance, priority-customer list, stock, crew or restoration commitment was inferred.

scenarioMatrix.summary: All ten canonical presets completed at all six required checkpoints for all eight services.
notes: Peak state severities at required checkpoints were storm 0.4483, pluvial 0.5958, river 0.2927, coastal 0, heat 0.6913, winter 0.4483, cyber 0.4306, earthquake 0.0072, wildfire 0.1146 and compound 0.9159.

At T+24 compound had rain 58.799 mm/h, inundation-stress amplitude 0.6011, wind 23.38 m/s, cyber disruption 0.3778, system pressure 0.5718, 19,256 modeled people under pressure and 303,409 cumulative event-attributable essential-service person-hours.

At T+72 compound retained inundation-stress amplitude 0.6011 and cyber disruption 0.0491, with severity 0.4824, pressure 0.4973, 15,935 people under pressure and 1,152,444 cumulative proxy person-hours.
All numerical values are deterministic derived scenario estimates, not observed local weather, flood depth, incident probability, outage, casualty or restoration data.

numericalInvariants.summary: Finite bounds, exact no-event semantics, determinism, monotonic cumulative burden, route bounds and local reconciliation pass.
notes: MUNICIPALITY_AUDIT_CODE=GM0753 pnpm audit:model passed both tests across 10 presets × 6 checkpoints × 8 services in 28.60 seconds on the focused run.
Every canonical preset at intensity zero produces exactly zero current severity, peak severity, affected population and event-attributable essential-service person-hours at every checkpoint.
Repeated frames are deterministic; state is finite and bounded; cumulative person-hours are monotonic; and route flow never exceeds effective logical capacity.
All local maps preserve 31,652 residents including exact zero for Heide; maximum population/service reconciliation error was 1.42e-14.
Changing among all eleven map layers leaves hazard, system pressure and affected population exactly invariant.

spatialPlausibility.summary: The generic major-river field and shared neighbourhood seed contradict Best's official flood/heat evidence and ignore an explicit fire source.
notes: River stress rises from zero at T+0 to 0.3331 at T+6 and 0.9464 at T+12, remaining 0.9464 through T+72; affected population is 10,074 at T+12, 11,242 at T+24 and 11,349 at T+48/T+72.

packages/sim-core/src/model.ts:430-461 measures the GM0753 centre against three coarse diagonal corridors and lines 642-647 turn that screen into direct water. E02 says this high-lying region has no direct flood danger and instead describes an indirect blocked-drainage pathway.

packages/sim-core/src/model.ts:3376-3390 applies municipality severity through one scenario/neighbourhood hash. Storm, pluvial, river, heat, winter, cyber and wildfire therefore have the identical exact neighbourhood order.

At pluvial T+24 the order starts Aarlesche Erven, De Leeuwerik, Villawijk, 't Zand and Hoge Akker; Breeven is 17/19, Wilhelminadorp 18/19 and Speelheide 19/19. E03 names the latter three among areas with water against buildings and says Villawijk is the one mapped location the municipality did not recognize in practice.

Heat uses the same order: Breeven is 17/19 even though E03 names it among Best's hottest areas, while Aarlesche Erven, De Leeuwerik and Villawijk rank first through third without support from the official heat analysis.

In a focused synthetic T+24 wildfire with source [5.383370097504299, 51.4904495404155] at the official centre of Heide, GM0753 direct-fire intensity is 0.4888 but source neighbourhood Heide ranks 6/19 at hazard 0.5332; Aarlesche Erven 2.745 km away ranks first at 0.5718. This proves local allocation ignores the selected source; it is not evidence of an observed fire.
Coastal direct inundation remains exactly zero and the canonical remote wildfire gives zero direct flame while separately exposing smoke/drought, correctly retaining scoped direct-zero semantics.

serviceDependencies.summary: All eight service balances and dependency ledgers are inspectable, but magnitudes are not calibrated to Best's providers, assets, tunnel or external care network.
notes: River T+24 availability was power 0.5339, water 0.6858, drainage 0.4435, gas 0.8386, telecom 0.6873, mobility 0.6180, facilities 0.6825 and supply 0.3816.
Compound T+24 availability was power 0.1570, water 0.7260, drainage 0.5573, gas 0.6697, telecom 0.4366, mobility 0.6942, facilities 0.1918 and supply 0.1968.
E02 supports dependency directions among vital systems but no authoritative source calibrates those exact availability, demand, delivery, backup or repair values for Best.

The graph has no named Enexis station/feeder, Brabant Water pressure zone, sewer catchment/pump, mobile network, rail tunnel system, hospital transfer, depot, supermarket stock or emergency-supply node.

All eight service views reuse the same six road-derived links and nominal total 1,450; emitted transferSemantics remains logical-proxy at packages/sim-core/src/model.ts:2038 and is never physical utility topology.
The street-detail utility adapter is explicitly Liander-only while Best's provider territory is Enexis, so it cannot fill Best's physical power/gas topology gap.

causalTrace.summary: Hazard, service and municipality explanation ledgers close and preserve scenario confidence, controls, dependency ordering and counterfactual scope.
notes: Hazard contributions sum to headline severity; each service baseline plus exact-stage deltas sums to availability; all eight weighted service-pressure contributions sum to municipality system pressure.
Dependency chains, drivers, local vulnerability/demand factors, recovery progress and service-restoration counterfactual deltas are finite and arithmetically closed.
Household preparedness changes modeled people/supply consequences after physical pressure rather than changing physical hazard fragility.
Operational controls and time-gated interventions are labeled scenario assumptions; shared road-derived utility flows remain logical proxies.

Event-attributable essential-service person-hours integrate weighted unmet-service pressure against a matched no-event baseline and are not observed outage-hours, casualties, displacement or welfare loss.

recovery72h.summary: Sustained-water and response-delay safeguards behave consistently, but unsupported forcing and absent operational resources prevent local recovery interpretation.
notes: Unsupported river forcing remains active at T+72: pressure is 0.3945, 11,349 people remain under pressure and cumulative proxy burden reaches 769,635 person-hours.

River T+72 keeps power, water, drainage, gas, telecom, mobility and supply at their T+24 values while facilities shifts from 0.6825 to 0.6653 through generic dependencies; this is not an operator or care forecast.
Pluvial water clears by T+48 and pressure falls from 0.1961 at T+24 to 0.0794 at T+72; compound retains 0.6011 generic water and pressure 0.4973 through T+72.

The two-week heatwave retains 25.64 degrees Celsius and drought severity 0.5982 at T+72 while affectedPopulation is zero; this threshold outcome must not be read as no residual health or water-demand burden.
E04 defines flexible monitoring, acute approximately three-day response and transition to long-crisis structures, but model interventions are not actual CoPI/ROT/municipal/operator decisions.
Actual tunnel access, rail operations, drainage controls, provider switching, roads, hospitals, crews, mutual aid, fuel, spares, staff, stocks and restoration estimates are unknown.

findings.summary: A coarse proximity corridor creates unsupported sustained direct Rhine/Meuse/IJssel inundation across Best.
findings.evidence: E02 states that the relatively high-lying Brabant-Zuidoost region has no direct flood danger and identifies an indirect mechanism in which major-river flooding to the north can block drainage from southern Brabant. packages/sim-core/src/model.ts:430-461 nevertheless measures Best's centre against three diagonal lines, and lines 642-647 emit direct municipality water. The canonical preset reaches internal inundation stress 0.9464 at T+12 and holds it through T+72, with 11,242 modeled people/191,870 event-attributable essential-service person-hours at T+24 and 11,349 people/769,635 person-hours at T+72. No selected dike breach, connected footprint, backwater/catchment model, level, arrival, duration or local depth supports this result.
findings.action: Mark GM0753's named-major-river result unsupported/Unknown and make its direct forcing numerically neutral until an expert-selected hydraulic footprint exists. Preserve blocked drainage, local/regional water, groundwater and pluvial mechanisms as unresolved rather than safe. The durable model must sample a named/versioned LIWO or water-board scenario and expose people/services only within its connected footprint.

findings.summary: The neighbourhood water map contradicts Best's official 70 mm/hour stress-test locations.
findings.evidence: E03 names nine areas with water against buildings and explicitly says Villawijk is the one mapped water-on-street result not recognized by the municipality in practice. At canonical pluvial T+24, however, the simulator ranks Villawijk third while documented Breeven, Wilhelminadorp and Speelheide rank 17th, 18th and 19th. Aarlesche Erven ranks first despite the 2022 product not validating it. packages/sim-core/src/model.ts:3376-3390 samples no rain-depth cell, terrain, sewer, surface flow or municipal validation; the exact same 19-neighbourhood order is used for storm, river, heat, winter, cyber and wildfire.
findings.action: Do not use current neighbourhood water ranks for deployment. Obtain the native machine surface behind Best's stress test or its successor, retaining the 70 mm/hour event, resolution, units, edition, no-data, municipal validation and licence. Use Klimaateffectatlas/AHN/IMWA/GWSW only as clearly scoped covariates. Add fixtures that preserve the official strong-vs-public-space classes, allow hazard footprints to differ and prevent Villawijk from being presented as practice-validated.

findings.summary: The local heat map reverses key areas in Best's official heat-island analysis.
findings.evidence: E03 reports a 0.05–3.5 degree Celsius heat-island range and identifies industrial areas 't Zand, Breeven and Heide, the area west of Salderes, and Centrum/Oud Best as hottest. The canonical T+24 heat map instead reuses the water/storm/cyber hash: Aarlesche Erven, De Leeuwerik and Villawijk rank first through third, while Breeven ranks 17/19. The model has no official heat raster, land cover, shade, building form or surface-material input; neighbourhood order therefore cannot support targeted cooling, welfare checks or facility decisions.
findings.action: Mark local heat ranking synthetic/unsupported until a versioned Best heat surface is sampled. Ingest the native municipal heat-island layer or a documented Klimaateffectatlas product with resolution, reference period/scenario, unit, edition, no-data, licence and uncertainty retained; use BGT/BRT land cover and CBS vulnerability only as disclosed factors. Test that known hot industrial/central areas respond to source cells rather than a shared hash.

findings.summary: An explicit Best wildfire source does not control the neighbourhood map of direct fire impact.
findings.evidence: E02 establishes nature fire as a real regional climate-linked risk; E03 documents drought and Best's green/sandy context. In a reproducible synthetic test, a T+24 source at [5.383370097504299, 51.4904495404155], the official centre of Heide, gives direct-fire intensity 0.4888, smoke 0.4607 and municipality severity 0.4884. Yet source neighbourhood Heide ranks only 6/19 at 0.5332 while Aarlesche Erven 2.745 km away ranks first at 0.5718. This is the same shared seed order as water and heat, proving local allocation ignores the selected source. The test is not evidence of an observed fire.
findings.action: Until polygon/source-aware fire allocation exists, label neighbourhood flame ranks unsupported and do not use them for dispatch. Prefer an authorized NIPV Risiko-index Natuurbranden export; otherwise combine BRT TOP10NL combustible land cover, an explicit ignition/perimeter and timestamped KNMI weather with inspectable fuel, wind, access and suppression assumptions. Tests must prioritize source-intersecting eligible cells and keep flame, smoke and drought separate.

findings.summary: Best's unique rail tunnel and underground station are reduced to an untyped station point and no rail dependency.
findings.evidence: E02 identifies the 2.6 km Best rail tunnel, including 900 m enclosed and 200 m depressed open track, as the only long rail tunnel in Brabant-Zuidoost. It crosses the built-up area, contains the underground station, has dedicated safety systems, an attack plan and rail-sector crisis planning. E05 contributes Best station and trace context, but the generated causal network contains only six road links. Winter T+24 mobility 0.3403 and storm T+24 mobility 0.3076 therefore do not use tunnel availability, rail timetable/rolling stock, smoke/evacuation constraints, alternative access or incident plans.
findings.action: Add the ProRail tunnel/trace/station geometry as non-causal official context now, clearly preserving the manual update cadence and CC0 licence. For a future tunnel or weather-disruption scenario, add a named rail/tunnel edge only with authorized safety-system, closure, evacuation and operational assumptions; never infer live tunnel capacity or publish sensitive response-plan detail.

findings.summary: Provider responsibility is public, but Best's physical utility topology, state and restoration capacity are not established.
findings.evidence: Live Stichting Mijn Aansluiting WMS point queries at Best's reference point returned Enexis for electricity/gas, Brabant Water for drinking water and Ziggo for fixed media, while drainage returned no polygon. E06 contributes nine De Dommel weirs but no public sewer pump/RWZI inside the boundary. Provider areas and static assets cannot establish feeder/pressure-zone connectivity, load, switching, pump state, mobile coverage, backup, priority customers, crews or restoration. apps/web/src/data.ts:837-925 offers Liander-only cable/station detail, which cannot fill the Enexis-area gap. All current service numbers remain synthetic.
findings.action: Keep provider and water objects affectsSimulation=false with coverage and timestamps visible. Integrate Enexis public static asset data only as clearly scoped context after verifying current catalogue licence/cadence; obtain licensed, security-reviewed operator exercise topology/state for causal use. Otherwise retain service-specific bounded priors, sensitivity controls and explicit Unknown operational state.

findings.summary: Best depends on external acute-care access, but facilities are not modeled as named capacity or patient-transfer nodes.
findings.evidence: E07 has no acute hospital in GM0753; the nearest listed 24/7 emergency departments are Catharina Ziekenhuis at 7.52 km and Máxima Medisch Centrum at 12.34 km by reference-point distance. The app's eight local KVK government points are coarse 2020 registry context and do not establish emergency function. Facilities availability falls to 0.1918 in compound T+24, but there is no hospital acceptance/diversion, ambulance route, tunnel/road access, staffing, bed, generator, pharmacy, care-home or home-care state behind that number.
findings.action: Use the annual CC0 RIVM hospital questionnaire as dated non-causal context and add route-aware external-care destinations only with clearly defined travel assumptions. Seek authorized GHOR/ROAZ exercise capacity and municipal vulnerable-facility continuity data; where unavailable, expose Unknown rather than inferring operation from a point or generic availability scalar.

findings.summary: Generic intervention buttons do not represent the authority and coordination structure used during Best's first 72 hours.
findings.evidence: E04 defines acute crisis as up to about three days, continuous monitoring, planning staff, flexible CoPI/ROT activation and distinct general-versus-functional authority. A mayor or safety-region chair can take general public-safety measures, while electricity, food and other functional sectors remain under their competent chain. Current generator, pump, traffic and medical-priority controls are time-gated scenario assumptions with deterministic effects; they are not actual GRIP activation, municipal decisions, operator switching or resource commitments.
findings.action: Keep controls explicitly hypothetical. Add an operational timeline separating signal, decision authority, action owner, prerequisite, dispatch/travel delay, resource quantity and observed confirmation. Offer an exercise-only Best/Brabant-Zuidoost playbook aligned with E04 without asserting that a named authority or operator has taken the action.

findings.summary: Weather, cyber and earthquake outputs are exercises, while important Best-specific transport risks fall outside the ten-preset contract.
findings.evidence: E02 supports storm, heat, winter, nature fire, extreme rain, vital-service and cyber relevance but not the model's exact magnitudes. Canonical earthquake uses a Groningen epicentre and peaks at only 0.0072 for Best; cyber is a configured process; weather is generated rather than driven by E08. Direct coastal water and canonical remote wildfire flame are coherently zero, but those scoped results do not mean no indirect coastal supply risk or no local fire risk. E02 separately identifies the Best rail tunnel, air, rail, road hazardous-material and airport-related incidents, which the ten natural-disaster/service presets do not simulate.
findings.action: Keep every preset labeled deterministic scenario, never forecast or probability. For observed/context mode, use timestamped KNMI products and the KNMI earthquake catalogue with validity/licence retained; require selected epicentre/ground-motion assumptions for earthquake and explicit targets for cyber. List omitted risks visibly and add them only as separately evidenced scenario families.

findings.summary: Identity, demography, boundary, neighbourhood, place, settlement and public-context provenance are inspectable and null-safe.
findings.evidence: E01 matches GM0753/Best, 31,652 residents, density 934, 6,561 residents aged 65 or older and 4,397 one-person households. All 19 neighbourhoods, one BAG place and three BRT settlements resolve; the 13-person neighbourhood rounding difference is disclosed. Missing district heat/public charging and suppressed cells remain null. E05–E08 objects retain publisher, URL, licence/edition and time/coverage semantics and affect simulation only where explicitly declared false.
findings.action: Retain edition, retrieval, licence, coverage and null semantics; refresh at source cadence and rerun focused plus national gates after every snapshot.

findings.summary: The complete deterministic, causal and layer-invariance contract passes for Best.
findings.evidence: The mandatory harness passes 10 presets × 6 checkpoints × 8 services; zero-intensity output is exact zero; local compound T+24 population/affected/service balances reconcile; ledgers close; person-hours are event-attributable against a matched no-event baseline; all eleven layer selections preserve state; zero population is retained; and every route says logical-proxy.
findings.action: Retain these assertions as regression gates while adding authoritative spatial adapters; do not weaken deterministic or exact-zero behavior to conceal calibration gaps.

provinceReviewFlags: Review every remaining Brabant-Zuidoost municipality receiving direct Rhine/Meuse/IJssel stress against the current regional statement of no direct flood danger and a selected connected scenario; preserve indirect blocked drainage and local water mechanisms as Unknown.

Replace shared neighbourhood hazard seeds across Noord-Brabant with licensed hazard-specific municipal/atlas surfaces, AHN terrain and water-board context while preserving event definition, resolution, no-data, edition and licence.
Audit tunnel, underground-station and airport-adjacent municipalities with typed mobility/evacuation context; static ProRail/NWB geometry cannot establish operational state or response capacity.
Coordinate Enexis, Brabant Water, municipal drainage, De Dommel, provider territories and public facilities as non-causal context unless authorized operational topology/state is supplied.

corrections.summary: Stop exposing Best's generic named-major-river proximity value as supported local inundation and require a selected connected scenario.

residualLimitations: The simulator is a deterministic planning stress test, not a KNMI forecast, warning, probability estimate, live incident picture, casualty model or operator outage forecast.
No approved Best LIWO/water-board connected depth, arrival, duration, defence, blocked-drainage, local-water or catchment grid is ingested; internal inundation stress is not measured local metres.
Suppressing unsupported Rhine/Meuse/IJssel forcing must not erase indirect blocked drainage from northern flooding, local groundwater, sewer overload, surface-water or extreme-rain mechanisms.

Best's 2022 climate stress test is authoritative planning context but not a live event or licensed native machine surface; Aarlesche Erven may also post-date the mapped analysis and remains Unknown rather than safe.
CBS neighbourhoods and deterministic seeds do not resolve buildings, terrain depressions, shade, paving, forests, fuels, sewers, water controls, households, visitors or individual vulnerability.
The public water layer is intentionally partial; nine weirs and zero listed sewer pumps/RWZI cannot be interpreted as Best's complete drainage system or operational state.

Provider polygons identify responsibility at one reference point, not full physical coverage, topology or state; fixed-media territory does not represent mobile coverage and drainage coverage is absent.
Liander-only open cable detail does not cover Enexis territory; no physical Enexis, Brabant Water, sewer, telecom, care or supply topology/state is available to the model.

All eight intermunicipal service layers reuse six road-derived logical corridors and cannot be interpreted as cables, pipes, pressure zones, radio backhaul, patient transfers, rail capacity or food routes.
Static NWB, ProRail and GTFS inputs do not establish live road/rail closure, traffic, timetable operation, tunnel safety state, evacuation throughput or repair access.
The unique Best tunnel lacks ventilation, egress, smoke, rolling-stock, incident-command and alternative-route state; sensitive attack-plan details were not inferred.
No acute hospital lies inside GM0753 in E07; straight-line distance to external hospitals is not ambulance travel time, acceptance, staffed capacity or diversion status.
Facilities and supply lack verified care-home/pharmacy roles, beds, staff, backups, supermarket/warehouse stock, depots, vehicles and continuity agreements.
Wildfire lacks a local incident perimeter, eligible fuel/moisture surface, wind-aware spread, suppression state and resource access; the Heide diagnostic is explicitly synthetic.
Earthquake lacks a selected local event, ground-motion surface, site response and asset fragility; the canonical Groningen event does not test a local Brabant earthquake.
Generic preparedness, demand, backup, network, repair and intervention multipliers are scenario controls rather than observed Best resources or commitments.
The crisis plan defines authority and flexible organization, not a guaranteed sequence, resource inventory or restoration service-level agreement for GM0753.

Six-hour checkpoints can miss cloudbursts, flash runoff, dispatch, tunnel evacuation and restrictions; the 72-hour horizon excludes prolonged displacement, contamination, public health, economic loss and reconstruction.
The ten canonical presets omit Best's officially documented tunnel incident and broader regional air, rail, road hazardous-material and other crisis types.
